newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chirac to back Spain on EMU at top security summit.
newsitem.headline: Chirac to back Spain on EMU at top security summit.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac meets Spanish Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar amid top security after a nearby bomb blast on Monday and will offer moral support for Spain's bid to join European monetary union.

Chirac, who sparked a diplomatic row with Rome last month by questioning Italy's chances of joining a single EU currency from the start in 1999, looks set to stick to a message of hope that both Spain and Italy will be ready in time.

"We hope that they will be there in 1999 while respecting the (Maastricht treaty) criteria," presidential spokeswoman Catherine Colonna told a news conference ahead of the summit in this southern port town.

Corsican separatists said they bombed the main post office in the French town of Aix-en-Provence early on Monday, a few hours before the Franco-Spanish meeting was to open in nearby Marseille. Police said the attack badly damaged the building but caused no injuries.

Colonna said France's attitude was consistent on Spain and Italy's preparations for monetary union and that Chirac would welcome Madrid's efforts to cut its budget deficit, one of the main terms for joining the European Union's single currency.
"He (Chirac) would like Spain to be in a position to meet the (economic) convergence criteria," in 1999, Colonna said.
Chirac hoped the largest number possible of European Union countries would be ready for the planned start of the "euro" currency in 1999, she added.
The Franco-Spanish summit will take place amid heightened security after the bomb attack in Aix-en-Provence, about 30 km (18 miles) from Marseille.
The "Historic Wing" of the Corsican National Liberation Front (FLNC) claimed responsibility for the bombing.
Interior Minister Jean-Louis Debre said in Paris 13 people had been detained on the Mediterranean island in a police swoop on Sunday and early Monday over a car bomb attack in July.
Hundreds of police mounted a major security operation in Marseille in advance of the arrival of the French and Spanish leaders, whose summit was due to start in the late afternoon.
The attack in Aix-en-Provence coincided with another attack on Corsica early on Monday which destroyed the private car of a senator.

It follows a spate of attacks on the French mainland which hit the mayoral office of Prime Minister Alain Juppe in the southwestern town of Bordeaux as well as law courts in Aix-en-Provence and Nimes.

An expert on terrorism, Roland Jacquard, said French authorities had established that there were links between the Corsican FLNC and ETA guerillas fighting the Spanish government for a separate Basque state.
The Franco-Spanish summit, which will also include finance, defence and foreign affairs ministers, was scheduled to start at 1625 GMT and continue Tuesday morning.
It was not immediately clear to what extent the talks might also focus on the plight of more than one million Hutu refugees in embattled eastern Zaire.
France has exhorted its partners in the European Union to be prepared to intervene to prevent a human disaster threatening the refugees in Kivu province in eastern Zaire.
But Paris first wants a clear international mandate and the European Union has said a ceasefire must declared before the flood of refugees caught in conflict there could be helped.

French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette on Monday poposed an international conference to study how to restore security in eastern Zaire to let refugees return to their camps, saying his psoposal was aimed at France's partners, including the United States, the European Union, the Organisation of African Unity (OAU) and Canada.
